title: Simultaneous finite coefficient polynomial lifts over an integer model
statement: Let $R,C,A,D$ be commutative rings with ring maps $\rho:R\to A$, $u:C\to A$ and $v:C\to D$. Suppose $C$ is finitely presented over $\mathbf Z$ [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. Put $T=R\otimes_{\mathbf Z}C$ with its $R$- and $C$-algebra structures and map $\tau:T\to A$, $r\otimes c\mapsto\rho(r)u(c)$, using [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]. Given any integer $n\geq0$ and elements $x_1,\ldots,x_n\in A\otimes_C D$, there exist integers $m_j\geq0$, elements $a_{jk}\in A$, $d_{jk}\in D$ for $1\leq j\leq n$, $1\leq k\leq m_j$, and a finite family $c_1,\ldots,c_s$ generating $C$ over $\mathbf Z$, such that $x_j=\sum_{k=1}^{m_j}a_{jk}\otimes d_{jk}$. Let $J=\{(j,k):1\leq j\leq n,1\leq k\leq m_j\}$ and $P=T[X_{jk}:(j,k)\in J]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. The homomorphism $\varphi:P\to A$ extending $\tau$ and sending $X_{jk}$ to $a_{jk}$ is compatible with both $R$ and $C$. The elements $1\otimes c_i$ generate $T$ over $R$, and their images together with the $X_{jk}$ generate $P$ over $R$; in particular $T$ and $P$ are of finite type over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Writing $\lambda:P\otimes_C D\to A\otimes_C D$ for $p\otimes d\mapsto\varphi(p)\otimes d$, the elements $z_j=\sum_kX_{jk}\otimes d_{jk}$ satisfy $\lambda(z_j)=x_j$. All tensor products are module tensor products [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] with their commutative algebra structures. No Noetherian or flatness hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Choose a finite presentation of $C$ over $\mathbf Z$ by [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], and let $c_1,\ldots,c_s$ be the images of its polynomial variables. Surjectivity of the presentation means that every $c\in C$ equals $q(c_1,\ldots,c_s)$ for some $q\in\mathbf Z[Y_1,\ldots,Y_s]$. Thus this finite family generates $C$ over $\mathbf Z$.

source.place: Tag 00F3, definition-finite-type, part (2): images of the variables of a finite presentation

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], each $x_j$ is a finite $C$-linear combination of pure tensors. Absorb each scalar into the first factor using $b(a\otimes d)=(u(b)a)\otimes d$. Enumerating the finitely many terms gives $x_j=\sum_{k=1}^{m_j}a_{jk}\otimes d_{jk}$. There are finitely many $j$, so these choices give a finite set $J$ of pairs $(j,k)$. A zero tensor may be represented by the empty sum; when $n=0$, take $J=\varnothing$.

source.place: Tags 00CV and 00CX, section-tensor-product and lemma-tensor-product: free-module quotient construction and bilinearity

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] over $\mathbf Z$ to $\rho:R\to A$ and $u:C\to A$; ring homomorphisms commute with the canonical integer maps. This constructs $\tau:R\otimes_{\mathbf Z}C\to A$ with $\tau(r\otimes c)=\rho(r)u(c)$. For each $c=q(c_1,\ldots,c_s)$ from step 1, the ring map $c\mapsto1\otimes c$ gives $1\otimes c=q(1\otimes c_1,\ldots,1\otimes c_s)$. Every tensor in $T$ is a finite sum of pure tensors by [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], absorbing integer scalars into $R$. Since $r\otimes c=(r\otimes1)(1\otimes c)$, every such sum is a polynomial over $R$ in the $1\otimes c_i$. Hence these elements generate $T$ over $R$.

source.place: Tag 034Y, lemma-descend-faithfully-flat-finite-presentation, final paragraph: integer-model base extension; Tag 00CX for finite sums

proof.text: Form $P=T[X_{jk}:(j,k)\in J]$. Give $A$ its $T$-algebra structure via $\tau$. The evaluation universal property in [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] gives a unique $T$-algebra homomorphism $\varphi:P\to A$ with $\varphi(X_{jk})=a_{jk}$. In particular $\varphi(r\otimes1)=\rho(r)$ and $\varphi(1\otimes c)=u(c)$, so $\varphi$ is compatible with both $R$ and $C$.

source.place: Tag 0367, lemma-finite-type-local-source-fppf-algebra, proof: make the finite coefficient enlargement explicit by polynomial variables

proof.text: Every element of $P$ is a finite sum of monomials in the $X_{jk}$ with coefficients in $T$, by [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Substitute the polynomial expressions for those coefficients from step 3. The result is a polynomial over $R$ in the images of the $1\otimes c_i$ and the $X_{jk}$. These form a finite family since $s$ and $J$ are finite. The generator characterization in [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra] therefore makes $T$ and $P$ finite type over $R$.

source.place: Tag 0367, lemma-finite-type-local-source-fppf-algebra, finite coefficient enlargement; Tag 00F3, definition-finite-type (1), algebra.tex

proof.text: In $A\otimes_C D$, take the ring maps $P\to A\otimes_C D$, $p\mapsto\varphi(p)\otimes1$, and $D\to A\otimes_C D$, $d\mapsto1\otimes d$. They agree on $C$: $\varphi(1\otimes c)\otimes1=u(c)\otimes1=1\otimes v(c)$ by step 4 and the balancing relation of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] over $C$ gives a ring map $\lambda:P\otimes_C D\to A\otimes_C D$ with $\lambda(p\otimes d)=\varphi(p)\otimes d$. Define $z_j=\sum_kX_{jk}\otimes d_{jk}$. Additivity and evaluation give $\lambda(z_j)=\sum_k\varphi(X_{jk})\otimes d_{jk}=\sum_ka_{jk}\otimes d_{jk}=x_j$. Empty sums obey the same identity. This proves every requested clause without a Noetherian or flatness assumption.
